skills.name: imagegen
skills.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.

interface.shortDescription: Generate or edit images for websites, games, and more
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $imagegen to make or edit an image for this project.

skills.name: openai-docs
skills.description: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex.
skills.shortDescription: Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, and self-knowledge; OpenAI APIs and ChatGPT Work. 'You'/'this app' means Codex only.

interface.shortDescription: OpenAI and Codex docs for models, skills, tasks, and setup
interface.defaultPrompt: Use OpenAI Docs for official docs lookup, questions about Codex itself or Codex surfaces, model selection, model migration, and prompt-upgrade work.

skills.name: review-agent
skills.description: Perform a read-only, defect-first review of a specified code change and return every actionable finding. Use when another agent delegates review of uncommitted changes, a base-branch diff, a commit, or custom review instructions.

interface.shortDescription: Find actionable bugs in code changes
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $review-agent to review the requested code changes and return actionable findings.

<collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

3: description: Use Yui to make an existing mathematical proof self-contained as structured NL0 with Audit A, then optionally translate it through typed interfaces into Lean with source-faithful Audit B. Supports NL0-only, translation from an accepted NL0, and full workflows. Do not infer proof correctness from schema checks or introduce unproved assumptions to close a goal.
4: ---
5: 
6: # Yui: rigorous proof development
7: 
8: Use the smallest requested track. Preserve the original problem, hypotheses,
9: definitions and proof route. The two stages share one specification and explicit
10: invalidation rules; completing stage one does not require stage two.
11: 
12: ## Select a stage
13: 
14: The invoking agent owns request/configuration collection and dispatch. Follow
15: [installed operation](references/operation.md) to identify explicit proof inputs,
16: ask once for missing active-phase model/reasoning/speed settings and, for a
17: full or translation request, an explicit per-case proof-worker count, then call
18: `scripts/yui.py run` (or prepare/execute). Retain settings already supplied by
19: the user; do not call a separate intent-classification model. Do not silently
20: choose a worker count from defaults or `auto`; obtain a positive integer or
21: the user's explicit confirmation of a proposed number. NL0-only requests need
22: no proof-worker question. NL0/Audit A and
23: Lean preparation/proofs/assembly/Audit B have separate phase profiles. The user
24: does not prepare queues, task packets or controller jobs manually.
25: For an ordinary foreground request, follow execution through its actual final
26: result; `DISPATCHED` is not completion. Use detached execution when requested or
27: when continuing to observe its owned run explicitly, and retain working cancel
28: instructions. A frozen author/proof/reviewer stage performs only its assigned
29: role; it does not redispatch the whole workflow.
30: 
31: Default permanent output is `<problem-directory>/rigorous-proof/<run-id>/`,
32: outside the installed skill. Multiple problems own separate outputs, contexts,
33: queues and ledgers. Use normal local repair unless a first-pass measurement is
34: explicitly requested. Runtime and software controls are fully inside this skill;
35: no repository example/support directory or old test result is required.
36: Positively identified temporary remote-service failures retry within the same
37: isolated thread, preserving its drafts and tool receipts. Keep the selected
38: profile and record every fault/wait; use [operational recovery](references/operation.md#remote-service-recovery)
39: for backoff, cancellation and explicit continuation of an already exited run.
40: 
41: 1. **NL0 and Audit A.** Use [Audit A's shared acceptance requirements](references/audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
42:    as the single mathematical standard for both author and auditor.
43:    Read [the NL0 stage](references/nl0-stage.md),
44:    [format](references/nl0-format.md), [self-containment](references/self-containment.md),
45:    [authoring](references/nl0-authoring.md), and Audit A's role-specific execution protocol.
46:    Read [external-source review](references/external-theorems.md) for citations
47:    and [logical packaging](references/logical-rules.md) for local assumptions.
48:    Use `scripts/nl0.py`; its explicit accounting is not a mathematical prover.
49:    Controllers and reviewers follow [completion and local repair](references/review-execution.md)
50:    for serial audit coverage, exact evidence inheritance and stage boundaries.
51: 2. **Translate an accepted NL0 and run Audit B.** Verify the supplied Audit A
52:    authority and exact source version first; do not reconstruct or re-audit an
53:    unchanged proof. Start with [minimal translation](translation/references/minimal-translation.md).
54:    Read [translation](translation/references/stage.md),
55:    [the working sequence](translation/references/integrated-workflow.md), and
56:    [Audit B](translation/references/audit-b.md). Operators use
57:    [execution and file-based control](translation/references/execution-protocol.md)
58:    for parallel queues, status and stops; workers need only their frozen packet.
59:    After local proofs complete, the serial postprocessing author follows
60:    [assembly and source-facing export](translation/references/assembly.md),
61:    then hands actual checked evidence to a separate independent Audit B reviewer.
62:    Use
63:    `translation/scripts/source_preparation.py` for bounded shared extraction,
64:    then `workflow.py` for source/IR freeze, proof work and final gates.
65: 3. **Full workflow.** Complete track one, then track two. A changed mathematical
66:    statement or new theorem returns to the affected NL0/Audit A boundary.
67: 
68: ## Mathematical invariants
69: 
70: - Accepted NL0 is a complete natural-language proof relative to explicit H/E/M,
71:   fixed logic and its hash-bound verified background supplement. Important
72:   tools remain explicit; ordinary correct elementary reasoning needs no
73:   exhaustive calculation chain. See [background notes](references/background-notes.md).
74: - Within NL0, each inference uses only its direct inputs, global definitions and explicitly
75:   established in-scope local facts or positively checked node-local background
76:   notes. Notes never add H or repair a substantive gap. Source papers and producer proof bodies do
77:   not fill gaps in a task packet.
78: - Preserve one global mathematical identity while allowing local Lean views.
79:   Actual cross-view conversions need checked proofs. In stage two, the pinned
80:   Mathlib environment is freely available without NL0 M registration.
81: - Shared mathematical extraction is a bounded local change at translation entry.
82:   Review its new producer and substitution cuts; inherit unchanged evidence.
83:   Freeze the revised NL0 before final IR and worker packets.
84: - Local conditional bodies may run concurrently. Assembly must discharge every
85:   internal dependency with an actual checked proof; conditional checks alone
86:   are not a final result.
87: - Audit B checks every external E and the complete target P, including its
88:   hypotheses, against actual Lean types and relevant definitions. Supply short
89:   direct/equivalent correspondence explanations; an independent reviewer verifies
90:   them. Check fresh Lean closure and trust, without a Mathlib-to-NL0 use ledger.
91:   Neither author notes nor a compiler pass are semantic approval.
92: - Stop on a judged substantive mathematical gap. Ordinary expansion and local
93:   verifiable corrections remain allowed. Difficulty or elapsed time does not
94:   establish that a mathematical claim is false.
95: 
96: ## Clean execution and accounting
97: 
98: Operators use [execution terminology](references/terminology.md) to distinguish
99: Codex conversations, native subagents, Yui jobs, worker slots and controllers.
100: Use the logical phase names **NL0 worker**, **preprocessing worker**,
101: **formalization workers (N slots)** and **postprocessing worker**. A logical
102: worker may contain several separate author/reviewer threads and program steps;
103: N limits only concurrent local Lean proof jobs.
104: Report executor termination separately from mathematical acceptance.
105: 
106: Read [isolation](references/isolation.md) and [measurement](references/measurement.md)
107: before any model test or benchmark. Run model authoring, planning, proof and
108: review stages through the isolated carrier. The interactive developer's memory,
109: other personal skills, expert packages, old task outputs and hidden reference
110: proofs are never an input source for these stages.
111: 
112: The Yui arm receives only the declared Yui rules and task material. The direct

15:

29: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
30: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
31: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.

34:

36: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
37: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P

41:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.

44:    no external inputs, record that fact.

46:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
47:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.

49:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
50:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.

53: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0

63: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.

66:

68: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M

70: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.

72: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
73: permissions to use a library theorem.

76: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
77: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
78: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
79: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
80: require returning to the affected source boundary.

86: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
87: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
88: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual

90: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
91: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
92: expected type for the actual inspected type.
93:

100: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.

104: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most

106: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
107: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
108: 
109: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
110: 
111: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
112: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
113: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
114: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool

121: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided
122: cold whole-workflow success or measured acceleration. Changing proofs or source
123: requires the appropriate new checks, rather than this review-only path.

127: `Proof.lean` before adding inspection. It checks E/P against their declared
128: encoded types, modulo definitional equality and bijective universe renaming.
129: It does not prove equivalence between natural-language text and Lean.
130: Distinct universes must not be collapsed; changed types or hypotheses must not
131: be normalized away. Source fidelity remains the independent reviewer's job.
132:

134: local axiom/opaque substitute or undeclared foundation may be introduced.
135: Local bodies still compile against their own task inputs and the pinned
136: library; every required producer must exist. Assembly, inspection and semantic
137: review have separate recorded outcomes.
138:

143: semantic review yields `AUDIT-B-PASSED`; a fragment yields at most the explicitly
144: scoped development verdict. Neither proves external publications in Lean or
145: establishes formalizer speedup. Preserve failures and report actual costs."}
